outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the positive-curvature case of Hopf’s sign conjecture has been claimed false in dimension six (S³×S³, arXiv:2609.11980, 6 Sep 2026, metric and proof credited to the ‘Odin Automatic AI Research Agent’), and the product form has been claimed false by a human-authored S²×S² preprint (arXiv:2608.19068, 19 Aug 2026) and by an AI-credited S²×S³ preprint (arXiv:2608.22133, 22 Aug 2026); none of these has a referee report or independent human check that I could find, one automated reviewer reports a Mathematica-dependent flaw in the S²×S² argument, and the negative and nonpositive sign conjectures remain open, with only restricted-class results posted in 2024–2026.
problem_asks: Unpacked from the statement (‘The Hopf conjectures relating the curvature and Euler characteristic of higher-dimensional Riemannian manifolds’), written before weighing any event. (a) Positive-curvature sign conjecture: every closed even-dimensional Riemannian manifold M^(2n) with everywhere positive sectional curvature has χ(M) > 0. (b) Nonnegative-curvature version: closed even-dimensional M with sec ≥ 0 has χ(M) ≥ 0. (c) Negative-curvature sign conjecture: closed M^(2n) with sec < 0 has (−1)ⁿ χ(M) > 0; and the nonpositive version: sec ≤ 0 gives (−1)ⁿ χ(M) ≥ 0. Parts (a)–(c) are asked in every even dimension, with the statement’s ‘higher-dimensional’ pointing at dimensions 2n ≥ 6; dimension 2 is Gauss–Bonnet and dimension 4 is the known case. SCOPE QUESTION, recorded not decided: the Wikipedia Hopf-conjecture article, which the bullet most likely links, also lists (d) the product conjecture — no direct product of two closed positive-dimensional manifolds admits a metric of positive sectional curvature, best-known case S²×S² — which concerns curvature but not Euler characteristic; and (e) Thurston’s aspherical conjecture, (−1)ᵏ χ(M^(2k)) ≥ 0 for closed aspherical manifolds (with Charney–Davis’s piecewise Euclidean analogue). The article also lists a degree-one self-map statement and an unrelated Eberhard Hopf conjecture on conjugate points, which I did not research as they bear on neither curvature nor Euler characteristic.

events.what_happened: Shengtao Guo, Ethan X. Fang and Junwei Lu, arXiv:2609.11980 (math.DG), ‘A Metric with Positive Sectional Curvature on S³×S³’. Claims a smooth Riemannian metric with strictly positive sectional curvature on S³×S³ and states that, since S³×S³ is even-dimensional with Euler characteristic zero, this disproves the positive-curvature case of Hopf’s sign conjecture. The abstract ends: ‘The metric and the proof were discovered by the Odin Automatic AI Research Agent.’ The introduction has a passage headed ‘The role of AI in this proof’ containing: ‘Odin Automatic AI Research Agent was used to construct the metric and the proof.’ The paper cites a companion repository, github.com/shengtaoguo/s3xs3-curvature-calculations, which contains Python 3.11 exact-arithmetic checks. The introduction also cites Püttmann–Searle to say a positively curved metric on S³×S³ must have a finite isometry group. Read via a summarising fetch of the arXiv HTML and abstract page; the raw PDF was not readable with my tools.
events.revisions: v1 6 Sep 2026 only, per the arXiv abstract page as fetched.
events.delivers: A metric with everywhere strictly positive sectional curvature on S³×S³ (dimension 6, χ = 0). If verified, the positive-curvature case of the sign conjecture (sec > 0 on a closed even-dimensional manifold forces χ > 0) fails in dimension 6. S³×S³ is a direct product of two closed positive-dimensional manifolds, so the same metric would also contradict the product form as the Hopf-article summary words it. The abstract does not say so; that is my logical reading, not the authors’. Restricted to strict positivity: it says nothing about nonnegative curvature, Ric₂, or negative curvature.
events.remains: Part (b), the nonnegative sign statement, and part (c), the negative and nonpositive sign statements, in all even dimensions, which this event does not touch. Part (a) is refuted in dimension 6 if the metric is valid, and part (d) is refuted by the same metric on the product S³×S³ under the same proviso. Part (e) is untouched.
events.time_since_posted: 36 days as of 12 Oct 2026. Searches (arXiv, MathWorld, news, the Wikipedia AI-discoveries list, Tao/Quanta/Mathstodon queries) found no referee outcome, correction, or expert commentary on this preprint.

machine_checked.system: Python 3.11 scripts with exact rational-arithmetic checks in the companion repository (verification/; the README says success prints ‘VERIFIED:’). Not a proof assistant.

events.directly_checkable: Checkable in principle. The paper reduces positivity to explicit second- and third-order curvature coefficients on the zero set of a background metric (two diagonal Cheeger deformations of the product metric, a normal homogeneous metric on SU(2)³/ΔSU(2)), and the companion code evaluates the identities over ℚ(z). I did not run the code or audit the reduction, so this is checkable but not checked by me.
events.doubts: No specific error identified in any source I could read. Reasons for caution, each with its basis: (1) no referee, journal, or third-party verification found; (2) correctness rests on the authors’ own code (11 commits, no license shown on the repository page), which I did not run; (3) the construction uses the same third-order deformation method as Brendle and Hung’s S²×S² metric, which an automated reviewer is reported to have flagged for a Mathematica-dependent step (second-hand, see the Brendle–Hung event); (4) the AI attribution comes with no account of the agent’s workflow, prompts, budget, or human checking beyond the one introduction sentence; (5) the footnote lists Junwei Lu in the Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. That bears on the team’s background in geometry, and is not evidence against the result.
events.direction: Cuts against the positive-curvature sign conjecture in dimension 6. It asserts a closed even-dimensional manifold with strictly positive sectional curvature and χ = 0, so, if valid, it contradicts ‘positive sectional curvature ⇒ χ > 0’ in that dimension. It does not bear on the nonnegative or negative sign conjectures.
events.object: A smooth Riemannian metric with everywhere strictly positive sectional curvature on S³×S³ (the main theorem). Explicit rather than non-constructive, as I read the introduction: g_τ = g₀ + τ(…) + τ²(…) + τ³ f̃ g₀, a perturbation of a background g₀ (two diagonal Cheeger deformations of the product metric, normal homogeneous on SU(2)³/ΔSU(2)) with fixed algebraic coefficients. Positivity is shown by checking the second- and third-order curvature coefficients on the zero set of g₀, with the algebraic identities evaluated exactly. I did not read the explicit coefficients.

events.what_happened: Simon Brendle and P. K. Hung (listed on arXiv as ‘S. Brendle, P.K. Hung’; search summaries give Pei-Ken Hung), arXiv:2608.19068, ‘A metric on S²×S² with positive sectional curvature’. Theorem 1.1: there exists a metric on S²×S² with positive sectional curvature. Method: start from the standard product metric, perform a Cheeger deformation to a nonnegatively curved Cheeger–Müter metric (the background is half of it), then add a third-order perturbation whose top term is 6χg, with χ fixed by a condition on a special torus. The proof splits by the sign of a constant μ. The abstract says ‘some of which have been carried out with the aid of Mathematica’ and ‘The Mathematica code is attached to this submission.’ The v2 comment says typographical errors in the manuscript and in the Mathematica notebook were corrected. Read via a summarising fetch of the arXiv abstract page and HTML v2; the raw PDF was not readable, and the Mathematica notebook was not retrieved.
events.revisions: v1 19 Aug 2026; v2 24 Aug 2026 (current; corrects typographical errors in the manuscript and the Mathematica notebook). Whether v2 fixed the step flagged by the automated reviewer is not established.
events.delivers: A metric of positive sectional curvature on S²×S², a direct product of two closed 2-manifolds, which contradicts the product form (no direct product of two closed positive-dimensional manifolds admits positive sectional curvature), if the proof is correct. Says nothing about the Euler characteristic: χ(S²×S²) = 4 > 0, so the sign conjectures are not engaged. Restricted to S²×S².
events.remains: Parts (a), (b), (c) and (e) are untouched. Part (d) is refuted for S²×S² as a single instance if the proof holds; the product form as a universal claim fails with that one instance.

events.directly_checkable: Partly. The background metric and the first two perturbation terms are explicit tensors built from constants λ_c and λ_d. The third-order function χ is fixed by a condition involving a Laplacian on a torus; I read that its existence follows from elliptic theory but did not confirm it. Positivity is claimed for small s. The notebook was not retrieved, and the authors’ publications page returned HTTP 403.
events.doubts: (1) The only critical check found is the automated Refine report, known second-hand, that a second-order positivity step depends on a Mathematica bug. I could not establish whether v2 fixed it. (2) No independent recomputation found. (3) The S³×S³ and S²×S³ preprints by other authors build on the same method; they are not independent checks. (4) MathWorld hedges: ‘if the proof is verified’. (5) A single-author note on almost-positive metrics on S²×S² (arXiv:2608.20888) does not verify this metric; a search summary of it says that author’s own attempt at a simpler explicit construction was not successful, which I did not confirm.
events.direction: Cuts against the product form, positive sectional curvature on the direct product S²×S², if verified. Silent on the sign conjectures: χ(S²×S²) = 4 is consistent with them.
events.object: A smooth metric on S²×S² with strictly positive sectional curvature (Theorem 1.1). Construction: background = half of the Cheeger–Müter metric; perturbation g̃_s = g + s·h⁽¹⁾ + s²·h⁽²⁾ + s³·h⁽³⁾, with h⁽¹⁾ and h⁽²⁾ explicit tensors built from constants λ_c and λ_d, and h⁽³⁾ = 6χg, where χ is fixed by a third-variation condition equal to a nonzero constant μ plus the Laplacian of χ on a torus Σ. Positivity holds for small s. Partly explicit: the existence of χ comes from an elliptic equation, as I read it.

events.what_happened: Shengtao Guo, Ethan X. Fang and Junwei Lu, arXiv:2608.22133, ‘A Metric with Positive Sectional Curvature on S²×S³’. Main theorem: S²×S³ admits a Riemannian metric with strictly positive sectional curvature. Method, per the paper’s summary: view S²×S³ as a principal circle bundle over S²×S²; start from a nonnegatively curved connection metric; perturb it by the real part of a global complex-valued symmetric 2-tensor; use a Gauss-equation argument along the circle fibres as they shrink. The paper says its construction differs from Brendle–Hung’s, which deforms the four-dimensional base. The abstract ends ‘The metric and the proof are discovered by the Odin Automatic AI Research Agent.’ The introduction says ‘Odin Automatic AI Research Agent was used to discover the Riemannian metric and the proof that it has positive sectional curvature.’ The main theorem’s introduction does not mention Hopf’s conjectures. Read via a summarising fetch of the abstract page and HTML v2 (about 128k characters, of which the first 100k were summarised).
events.delivers: A positively curved metric on the direct product S²×S³ of two closed positive-dimensional manifolds, which contradicts the product form as stated, if verified. It is silent on the Euler characteristic: S²×S³ has odd dimension 5, so the even-dimensional sign conjecture is not engaged. Whether the paper frames this as a product-form counterexample is for the judging pass; its own introduction does not say so.
events.remains: Parts (a), (b), (c) and (e) are untouched. Part (d) is already refuted by the S²×S² instance if that holds; the S²×S³ instance is a second one.

events.directly_checkable: Checkable in principle: an explicit construction from a circle-bundle connection metric and a global symmetric 2-tensor. Not checked by me. I did not find the verification method in the portions I read.

events.what_happened: Yuhang Liu, arXiv:2608.20888, ‘Almost Positive Sectional Curvature with Bounded Geometry on S²×S²’. Abstract (summarised): for a fixed open ball U and every ε > 0, a smooth metric on S²×S² whose sectional curvature is positive outside a closed set S_ε of relative volume less than ε, exceeds 1 on U, is bounded below by −ε and above by a constant independent of ε, with uniform volume, diameter and injectivity-radius bounds. Built from the product of unit round metrics, a conformal factor from smoothing a height function on each sphere, a second conformal deformation and a diffeomorphism. The comment reads ‘8 pages. AI generated and human verified.’ The abstract says: ‘The main content of this paper is generated by ChatGPT 5.6 and verified by the author.’ Single version, submitted 21 Aug 2026.
events.delivers: Almost-positive sectional curvature on S²×S²: positive outside a set of small relative volume, with a small negative part. This is a weaker hypothesis than everywhere-positive sectional curvature, so it does not settle the product form as stated. It addresses an analogue (a small exceptional set and a bounded negative part), not the universal statement.
events.remains: All of problem_asks as stated. The product form is not settled by this event, and nor are the sign conjectures.

events.what_happened: Ya Deng and Botong Wang, arXiv:2405.12012, ‘Linear Chern-Hopf-Thurston conjecture’. Proves the Chern–Hopf–Thurston sign inequality (−1)ⁿ χ(X) ≥ 0 for a closed aspherical manifold X of dimension 2n when X is a complex projective manifold whose fundamental group has an almost faithful linear representation over any field. A stronger statement for large π₁ uses perverse sheaves. The method uses a vanishing cycle functor for multivalued one-forms, non-abelian Hodge theory, and period maps. The abstract does not mention Singer’s conjecture. Read via the abstract page.
events.delivers: The nonstrict inequality (−1)ⁿ χ ≥ 0 for closed aspherical complex projective manifolds whose π₁ has an almost faithful linear representation. Restricted to that class, and nonstrict. It carries no curvature hypothesis. The nonpositive Hopf statement is a special case only for those nonpositively curved closed manifolds that lie in this class, which I did not check.
events.remains: Part (e), the general aspherical sign inequality, the strict version, and the nonpositive Hopf statement for manifolds outside the linear complex projective class.

events.what_happened: Teng Huang and Weike Yu, arXiv:2607.13917, ‘L¹-Integrability of L²-Harmonic Forms and the Hopf Conjecture’. For complete simply connected manifolds with −K ≤ sec ≤ 0, proves an a priori L^∞ estimate by Moser iteration, and shows that an L²-harmonic form which is also L¹-integrable must vanish. For closed nonpositively curved M, the k-th L²-Betti number of the universal cover vanishes if and only if every L²-harmonic k-form is L¹-integrable. The abstract presents this as a criterion and does not claim to prove the Hopf conjecture; the phrase appears only in the title. Read via the abstract page.
events.delivers: An equivalence between vanishing of L²-Betti numbers and L¹-integrability of L²-harmonic forms, for closed nonpositively curved manifolds. This is an analytic reformulation on the Singer–Dodziuk route to the nonpositive sign statement, not a proof of any Hopf statement.

events.what_happened: Teng Huang and Weiwei Wang, arXiv:2507.15237, ‘Decomposition of the Curvature Operator and Applications to the Hopf Conjecture’. Theorem 1.3: for compact even-dimensional M of dimension 2n (n ≥ 2) with sec ≥ a > 0, or sec ≤ −a < 0, and a Weyl-tensor bound |W| below an explicit constant times a, the curvature operator is positive, or negative, and the Euler characteristic conclusion is strict: χ > 0, or (−1)ⁿ χ > 0. The abstract says the results ‘confirm the Hopf conjecture for manifolds with sufficiently small Weyl curvature’. Theorem 1.2, as the authors state it: the Hopf conjecture holds for all compact locally conformally flat manifolds of even dimension. The abstract also reports new rigidity results under harmonic Weyl conditions. Versions: v1 21 Jul 2025; v2 25 Jul 2025. Read via the abstract page and HTML v2 (first 100k of about 103k characters).
events.delivers: Restricted-class confirmations of the positive and negative sign conjectures under a Weyl-smallness hypothesis that depends on the pinching constant, and, as the authors state, of the sign conjecture for all compact locally conformally flat even-dimensional manifolds. These classes are restricted, and nothing here settles the general sign conjectures. The LCF claim is the authors’ and I did not check its proof.
events.remains: The general sign conjectures in all even dimensions without the Weyl or LCF hypotheses, and the nonnegative case unless covered by these classes.

events.what_happened: Lee Kennard, Lawrence Mouillé and Jan Nienhaus, arXiv:2507.16936, ‘On Hopf’s conjecture and positive second intermediate Ricci curvature’. If a closed manifold with Ric₂ > 0 has dimension divisible by four and an effective isometric torus action of rank at least ten, then its Euler characteristic is positive. Key tool: an extension of Kennard’s Four Periodicity Theorem. The summary of the paper says the conclusion of the conjecture is known to fail under weaker curvature assumptions, including Ric₂ > 0 without symmetry, and that examples on S³×S³ (with T³) and S⁷×S⁷ (with T⁴) show the dimension and symmetry hypotheses cannot simply be dropped. Read via the abstract page (the summary of the examples is from the search summary and the introduction, not checked line by line). Single version, 22 Jul 2025.
events.delivers: Positive Euler characteristic for closed manifolds with Ric₂ > 0 in dimension divisible by four, with a torus of rank at least ten. A weaker-curvature analogue of part (a), restricted by dimension and symmetry. It settles nothing in problem_asks.
events.remains: Part (a) with no symmetry hypothesis, parts (b) and (c) in general, and the Ric₂ analogue outside the symmetry class.

events.what_happened: Lawrence Mouillé, arXiv:1911.03491, ‘Positive intermediate Ricci curvature on products of homogeneous spaces’. The abstract says it constructs metrics with Ric₂ > 0 on products of positively curved homogeneous spaces, and argues that the Hopf conjectures, among others, fail in the Ric₂ > 0 setting. Versions: v1 8 Nov 2019; v2 19 Apr 2020; v3 24 Nov 2020; v4 3 Mar 2021, marked ‘(withdrawn)’. The arXiv notice says ‘A newer version of this paper has been withdrawn by Lawrence Mouillé’. A fetch of the unversioned abstract page gave the reason as a mistake in Lemma 4.5 making Theorem 4.1 incorrect; a fetch of the v2 page found no stated reason. This conflict is unresolved.
events.revisions: v1 8 Nov 2019; v2 19 Apr 2020; v3 24 Nov 2020; v4 3 Mar 2021 (withdrawn). The date of the withdrawal notice is not shown.
events.delivers: Claimed Ric₂ > 0 examples on products, which would show the Euler-characteristic conclusion fails under Ric₂ > 0. Withdrawn, so it establishes nothing for the sign conjectures. Ric₂ is a weaker hypothesis than sec > 0, so it is an analogue.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.time_since_posted: Withdrawn version posted 3 Mar 2021, about 5 years 7 months before 12 Oct 2026.
events.doubts: The arXiv notice says the later version was withdrawn by the author. The stated reason conflicts between two fetches, so I record it as unresolved.

withdrawn.what: The v4 version (3 Mar 2021) is marked withdrawn; the notice says a newer version was withdrawn by the author.

events.direction: Under the weaker Ric₂ hypothesis, claimed to cut against the Euler-characteristic conclusion; withdrawn.

events.what_happened: A normal homogeneous metric on S³×S³ = SU(2)³/ΔSU(2) with positive second intermediate Ricci curvature, attributed in the S³×S³ preprint’s introduction to a construction of Wilking (quoted via a summarising fetch: ‘a construction of Wilking on S³×S³ with positive second intermediate Ricci curvature’). The Kennard–Mouillé–Nienhaus preprint (22 Jul 2025) also notes that S³×S³ admits a metric with Ric₂ > 0 and T³ symmetry. The original date of Wilking’s construction was not established by me.
events.delivers: A metric with Ric₂ > 0 on S³×S³ (χ = 0), which shows the Euler-characteristic conclusion fails under Ric₂ > 0 on a product with χ = 0. Weaker than sectional curvature, so an analogue. It does not decide the sec > 0 sign conjecture, which the 2026 Guo–Fang–Lu preprint addresses.
events.remains: Part (a) for sec > 0, which the Guo–Fang–Lu event addresses; parts (b) and (c).
events.time_since_posted: Original date not established. The Kennard–Mouillé–Nienhaus paper (22 Jul 2025) notes it.
events.directly_checkable: It is a homogeneous metric on an explicit quotient, checkable in principle. Not checked by me.
events.doubts: The attribution to Wilking and the Ric₂ statement come from a summary of the S³×S³ introduction and of the Kennard–Mouillé–Nienhaus summary; neither was checked against a primary Wilking source.
events.direction: Shows the Euler-characteristic conclusion fails under Ric₂ > 0 on S³×S³. Silent on sectional curvature.
events.object: A normal homogeneous metric on S³×S³ = SU(2)³/ΔSU(2) with Ric₂ > 0, admitting T³ symmetry (per Kennard–Mouillé–Nienhaus). Explicit homogeneous metric.
people: Wilking (as credited in the S³×S³ introduction)

events.what_happened: Jan Nienhaus, arXiv:2211.13151, ‘An improved four-periodicity theorem and a conjecture of Hopf with symmetry’. Proves the positive-sectional sign conjecture (a closed even-dimensional manifold with sec > 0 has χ > 0) under an isometric T⁴-action, improving the T⁵ hypothesis of Kennard, Wiemeler and Wilking. Second application: a classification of positively curved even-dimensional manifolds without odd rational cohomology that admit an isometric T⁶-action. Single version, 23 Nov 2022; no journal reference shown.
events.revisions: v1 23 Nov 2022 only, per the arXiv page.
events.delivers: The positive-sectional sign conjecture under an effective isometric torus action of rank 4. Restricted by symmetry rank. It does not address parts (b), (c), or the case without symmetry.
events.remains: Part (a) for manifolds with torus rank below 4 or no torus action; parts (b) and (c) in general.
events.time_since_posted: About 3 years 11 months as of 12 Oct 2026. Journal publication not established.
events.doubts: No third-party check of the argument found; the search summaries of later work treat it as a known improvement.
events.direction: Supports the positive sign conjecture in the restricted symmetric case.

events.what_happened: Lee Kennard, Michael Wiemeler and Burkhard Wilking, arXiv:2106.14723, ‘Splitting of torus representations and applications in the Grove symmetry program’. Proves Hopf’s positive-sectional sign conjecture for even-dimensional compact Riemannian manifolds with positive sectional curvature under the added assumption that the isometry group has rank at least five. v1 28 Jun 2021. Journal publication not established by me.
events.delivers: Part (a) under an isometry group of rank at least five. Restricted by symmetry.
events.remains: Part (a) without the rank-five hypothesis; parts (b) and (c).
events.time_since_posted: About 5 years 3 months as of 12 Oct 2026. Journal publication not established.
events.doubts: Journal status not established. The phrase ‘simply connected with effective T⁵-action’ from a talk summary is not in the abstract I read, so I do not record it as the hypothesis.
events.direction: Supports the positive sign conjecture under a large symmetry hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Lee Kennard, ‘On the Hopf Conjecture with Symmetry’, arXiv:1203.3808, v1 16 Mar 2012; published in Geometry & Topology 17 (2013), 563–593. Proves the positive-sectional sign conjecture under the assumption that a torus acts isometrically with dimension bounded below by a logarithmic function of the manifold dimension. The exact function was not read on the abstract page.
events.delivers: Part (a) under an effective isometric torus action of logarithmic rank. Restricted by symmetry.
events.remains: Part (a) without the torus assumption; parts (b) and (c).

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in volume 17 (2013), pages 563–593, per the arXiv page’s journal reference.

events.time_since_posted: Published 2013; predates the frozen revision.
events.direction: Supports the positive sign conjecture under a torus-symmetry hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Thomas Püttmann and Catherine Searle, ‘The Hopf conjecture for manifolds with low cohomogeneity or high symmetry rank’, Proc. AMS 130 (2002), no. 1, 163–166 (the year is given as 2001 on one source and 2002 on the volume listing; I use 2002 with year precision). arXiv:1207.4086 was posted 17 Jul 2012. Results: for an even-dimensional compact manifold with positive (or nonnegative) sectional curvature and an isometric action of a compact Lie group G with cohomogeneity condition k − (rank G − rank H) ≤ 5, the Euler characteristic is positive (or nonnegative); and for dimensions 4l+2 and 4l+4 with positive sectional curvature, χ > 0 if there is an effective isometric torus action of rank at least l.
events.revisions: Proc. AMS publication 2002; arXiv v1 17 Jul 2012.
events.delivers: Part (a) and its nonnegative analogue under compact Lie group symmetry with the stated cohomogeneity condition, and in dimensions 4l+2 and 4l+4 with torus symmetry rank at least l. Restricted by symmetry.
events.remains: Part (a) and (b) without the symmetry condition; part (c).

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society (journal)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in volume 130, issue 1 (2002), per the journal reference on the arXiv page.

events.time_since_posted: Published 2002; predates the frozen revision.
events.doubts: The year of publication differs between sources (2001 and 2002). Neither affects its place before the frozen revision.
events.direction: Supports the positive and nonnegative sign conjectures under the stated symmetry hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Hsiang and Kleiner (1989), as cited by MathWorld: a closed orientable positively curved 4-manifold with a nontrivial Killing field is homeomorphic to S⁴ or CP². MathWorld draws the consequence that a positively curved metric on S²×S² can have no continuous symmetry. Journal and page not checked by me; the 1989 year is from MathWorld.
events.delivers: A topological constraint on any positively curved 4-manifold with a continuous symmetry; it does not settle any part of the statement, since S²×S² is not excluded unless it has such a symmetry.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.time_since_posted: Published 1989 (per MathWorld); predates the frozen revision.
events.direction: A constraint on symmetric positively curved candidates for S²×S²; no direction on the conjecture as such.

events.what_happened: Chern (1955) handled the four-dimensional negative-curvature case through the Gauss–Bonnet–Chern formula: for closed 4-manifolds with negative sectional curvature the Gauss–Bonnet integrand is pointwise positive, so χ > 0. Attribution of the idea to Milnor is reported in some sources and not others. Known only from search snippets and a summary, not from the 1955 paper itself, which I did not open.
events.delivers: Part (c) in dimension four (χ > 0 for negative sectional curvature, and nonnegative for nonpositive). Settles dimension four of part (c).
events.remains: Part (c) in dimensions 2n ≥ 6.
events.time_since_posted: 1955; predates the frozen revision.
events.doubts: Attribution between Chern and Milnor is unresolved in my sources.
events.direction: Supports the negative sign conjecture in dimension four.

events.what_happened: Robert Geroch (1976), ‘On Geroch’s counterexample to the algebraic Hopf conjecture’ is the later discussion; the original gives a counterexample showing that positive sectional curvature does not make the pointwise Gauss–Bonnet–Chern integrand positive in higher dimensions. Known from search snippets (the AMS listing and a summary), not opened.
events.delivers: Shows the pointwise route to part (a) fails in dimensions above four. It does not decide the Euler-characteristic sign of any manifold.
events.remains: Parts (a), (b) and (c) in dimensions 2n ≥ 6.
events.time_since_posted: 1976; predates the frozen revision.
events.direction: Not a counterexample to the Euler-characteristic statement itself; a counterexample to the pointwise route.
events.object: Geroch’s algebraic counterexample concerns the pointwise sign of the Gauss–Bonnet–Chern integrand, not the Euler characteristic.

events.what_happened: Renato Bettiol, positive biorthogonal curvature on S²×S² (arXiv:1210.0043, posted October 2012 per the arXiv identifier; the journal reference is Proc. AMS 2014). Shows S²×S² satisfies an intermediate condition between Ric > 0 and sec > 0 in the biorthogonal sense, without nonnegative sectional curvature (per search summaries). Not opened.
events.delivers: Positive biorthogonal curvature on S²×S², which is weaker than sectional and does not give sec ≥ 0. It settles nothing in problem_asks.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks, since this is a different curvature notion.
events.time_since_posted: Posted October 2012, predates the frozen revision.
events.doubts: Not opened; the description is from search summaries.
events.direction: Not a sectional-curvature statement; no direction on the product form.

events.what_happened: Gromov introduced Kähler hyperbolicity and verified the negative-curvature sign statement for Kähler hyperbolic manifolds, including compact Kähler manifolds with negative sectional curvature, per a search summary. The original year was not established by me, and the paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Part (c) for Kähler hyperbolic manifolds (a restricted class).
events.remains: Part (c) for manifolds outside that class, and the other parts.
events.time_since_posted: Year not established by me.
events.doubts: Known only from a search summary.
events.direction: Supports part (c) in a restricted Kähler class.

disputes.summary: The sources differ on how firmly to treat the S²×S² claim. MathWorld hedges: ‘if the proof is verified’, and says the sign form is unaffected. The S³×S³ introduction (via a summarising fetch) says the product conjecture ‘has been disproved by Brendle and Hung’. The S²×S³ introduction says Brendle and Hung show S²×S² admits a positive metric. A search summary of a third, unopened preprint describes it as ‘resolving the Hopf conjecture’. I record the authors’ and MathWorld’s wording and do not pick one.

Three 2026 preprints by Guo, Fang and Lu credit the ‘Odin Automatic AI Research Agent’ with discovering the metric and the proof (S³×S³ and S²×S³), and a similarly credited Komlós-discrepancy paper (arXiv:2609.11189, not researched for this problem) suggests a pattern. I could not identify Odin as a system or lab from any source, and three searches returned only unrelated products named Odin. The claimed AI role is the authors’ own account, but no workflow or human-checking account has been found.

An anonymous Hacker News comment on the zeli.app page (27 Aug 2026) says the S²×S² Hopf problem was ‘solved by human mathematicians around the same time’. It is unattributed, and it is not a claim about the S³×S³ or S²×S³ results. I give it no weight beyond recording it.

The arXiv history of 1911.03491 marks v4 (3 Mar 2021) as withdrawn. One fetch reported a reason (an error in Lemma 4.5 making Theorem 4.1 incorrect); another fetch of the v2 page found no stated reason. Unresolved.

summary: I ran 35 searches and opened the arXiv abstracts or HTML of about 30 sources, plus MathWorld, the Wikipedia Hopf article and the Wikipedia list of AI mathematical discoveries. The bullet’s open content is parts (a)–(c), the sign conjectures. The 2026 events bear on them as follows. (1) Positive case, part (a): Guo, Fang and Lu, arXiv:2609.11980 (6 Sep 2026), claim a metric of strictly positive sectional curvature on S³×S³, which has χ = 0, so part (a) fails in dimension 6 if the claim holds. Its abstract and introduction credit the metric and proof to the ‘Odin Automatic AI Research Agent’. No source identifies that agent, and the authors describe no workflow. The paper relies on exact-arithmetic code in a public repository, which I did not run. (2) Product form, part (d): Brendle and Hung, arXiv:2608.19068 (19 Aug 2026; v2 24 Aug), give a positive-curvature metric on S²×S² by a Cheeger deformation followed by a third-order perturbation, with Mathematica code attached; an automated reviewer (Refine, reported second-hand from a thread I could not open, HTTP 402) flagged a dependence on a Mathematica bug in a second-order step. Guo, Fang and Lu’s arXiv:2608.22133 (22 Aug 2026) gives a positive metric on S²×S³, again credited to Odin, which bears on part (d) and not on the even-dimensional sign conjecture. Whether part (d) belongs to this bullet is a scope question I have flagged and not decided: the statement speaks of curvature and Euler characteristic, but the Wikipedia Hopf article lists the product form among the Hopf conjectures. (3) Restricted results: Kennard (2012/13), Püttmann–Searle (2002), Kennard–Wiemeler–Wilking (2021), Nienhaus (2022) and Kennard–Mouillé–Nienhaus (2025) prove part (a) under symmetry or Ric₂ hypotheses; Huang and Wang (2025) prove parts (a) and (c) under small-Weyl or locally-conformally-flat hypotheses; Deng and Wang (May 2024) prove a nonstrict aspherical inequality for complex projective manifolds with linear π₁; Huang and Yu (July 2026) give a criterion, not a proof. The negative case in dimension four is Chern (1955), and the general negative case remains open. (4) Discounted events: the S⁶ complex-structure claim by Alpöge (23 Aug 2026, credited to ‘Claude’, Lean-formalised by Alexeev, recorded as unverified by Scientific American) answers a different Hopf problem; Liu’s almost-positive S²×S² note (21 Aug 2026, ‘generated by ChatGPT 5.6’) is an analogue; Chen and Zhang’s S²×T² result concerns biorthogonal curvature. Close calls: whether the S³×S³ claim ‘settles’ the bullet depends on whether the bullet means the sign family as a whole. It refutes the positive case only, so parts (b), (c) and (e) remain open. Whether the AI-credited claims are load-bearing is answered by the authors’ own sentences (the agent ‘discovered’ the metric), but without any account of the workflow or human checking, so I record the sentences and not a judgement. Nothing from 2024 settles any part; the 2024 items are restricted cases. The Wikipedia AI-discoveries list (last edited 11 Oct 2026) has no entry for the S³×S³, S²×S³ or S²×S² results, only the S⁶ claim. The Wikipedia Hopf article (last edited 29 Aug 2026, read via a summarising fetch) names the product and aspherical conjectures and does not mention the 2026 preprints.
competing_reading: Read strictly, the S³×S³ claim is a counterexample to the positive case of the sign conjecture as the Wikipedia lead states it, and the S²×S² and S²×S³ claims refute the product form; on that reading the bullet has lost its positive and product cases, with the negative and nonnegative cases still open. The opposing reading treats all three as unrefereed preprints, with no independent recomputation, one automated report of a Mathematica-dependent flaw in the S²×S² argument (second-hand), and an AI attribution that names an unidentified agent without a workflow account, so none should yet count as a settlement. A third reading treats the product form as outside this bullet, which removes the S²×S² and S²×S³ events from scope and leaves only the S³×S³ claim.
what_would_settle_it: For part (a): a referee report or published verification of arXiv:2609.11980, and an independent recomputation of the exact checks in its companion repository. For part (d): a v3 or erratum of arXiv:2608.19068 showing whether the Mathematica-dependent step was fixed or is wrong, and an independent computer-algebra check of the S²×S² metric. For the AI attribution: the authors’ account of the Odin workflow and what was checked by hand, and identification of the agent’s lab and release. For the scope: a decision on whether the bullet includes the product conjecture and Thurston’s aspherical conjecture. For part (c): any new result on (−1)ⁿχ > 0 under negative curvature in dimension at least six.

dead_ends: Three searches for an ‘Odin’ automatic AI research agent returned unrelated products: an Odin AI desktop agent with review pages, the getodin.ai enterprise agent platform, an Odin graph-intelligence library on arXiv, and HockeyStack’s Odin. None is the agent credited in the Guo–Fang–Lu preprints, and no lab or release is identified.

Searches for expert reaction (Terence Tao, Quanta, Mathstodon, MathOverflow, news coverage) on the S³×S³, S²×S³ and S²×S² claims found no commentary, verification or refutation beyond the automated Refine report (second-hand).

No Lean or Mathlib formalisation of the positive-curvature sign conjecture or of the S²×S² product claim was found. The Google DeepMind Formal Conjectures repository was searched only through search results, and no Hopf entry was found; I did not open the repository.
Searches for AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, GPT-5 and Gemini in connection with the positive-curvature conjecture found no AI-credited result beyond those listed in events.
The Wikipedia AI-discoveries list (edited 11 Oct 2026) has no entry for the S³×S³, S²×S³ or S²×S² results. Its only Hopf entry is the S⁶ complex-structure claim.
Searches for 2024 settlements of the sign conjectures found none. The 2024 items are restricted cases (Deng–Wang) and revisions of pre-2024 work (Di Cerbo–Pardini, Albanese–Di Cerbo–Lombardi).
Cao–Tran (pinched four-manifolds) was searched for an S²×S² obstruction. The search did not locate the claimed inequality in the form described, so I did not record it.
Brendle’s publication page returned HTTP 403, so the Mathematica notebook for arXiv:2608.19068 could not be located.
The PDFs of 2609.11980, 2608.19068 and alpo.ge/s6.pdf returned binary content that my tools could not read; the HTML versions were used instead, and they were read through summarising fetches.

incomplete: (1) The raw text of arXiv:2609.11980, arXiv:2608.19068 and alpo.ge/s6.pdf was not readable with my tools (binary PDF). The HTML versions were read through a summarising fetch in two passes, one covering the first 100,000 characters and one covering the rest, so every quotation from these papers is a relayed quotation and should be checked against the source; the Odin sentences were confirmed in two separate passes. (2) The Ben Golub X thread (Refine report) returned HTTP 402 and was not read; the description of the reported Mathematica bug is second-hand, and the identification of the preprint it concerns is my inference. (3) I did not check whether arXiv:2608.19068 v2 fixed the step the automated reviewer flagged. (4) The Mathematica notebook and the S³×S³ Python checks were not run or audited. (5) The S⁶ claim’s manuscript and the Alpöge X post were not readable; its AI account is relayed through OfficeChai and Scientific American. (6) Pre-2024 events Chern (1955), Geroch (1976), Hsiang–Kleiner (1989), Bettiol (2012), Gromov’s Kähler hyperbolicity and Wilking’s Ric₂ construction were established from search snippets or from another paper’s summary and are marked opened false or lack a date. (7) The Wikipedia Hopf article was read through a summarising fetch; its list of conjectures is paraphrased. (8) Journal publication status is established only where the arXiv page gives a journal reference. (9) The Huang–Wang locally-conformally-flat theorem and the Mouillé withdrawal reason are unresolved as recorded above. (10) Scope: the product conjecture and Thurston’s aspherical conjecture are researched but their membership in this bullet is not decided.
